chunks: My father (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us, he said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, he said: Abu Ja'far Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa and Musa ibn Ja'far ibn Abi Ja'far al-Baghdadi narrated to us, from Abu Talib Abdullah ibn al-Salt al-Qummi, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from Dawud ibn Abi Yazid, who said: al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him) said:
When the sun sets, then the time of Maghrib has entered.

key_terms.غابت الشمس: The setting/disappearance of the sun below the horizon
key_terms.وقت المغرب: The time of Maghrib, the evening prayer performed after sunset

ai.seo_question: When does the time for Maghrib prayer begin according to Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) establishes a clear jurisprudential ruling about the commencement of Maghrib prayer time. This hadith, narrated in a scholarly assembly in Ramadan 367 AH, defines the beginning of the Maghrib prayer period as the moment the sun fully disappears below the horizon. The ruling clarifies the Shia position that the setting of the sun's disc marks the entry of Maghrib time.
word_analysis: may He have mercy on him

en.bilal-muhammad: My father (rh) narrated to us. He said: Sa`d b. `Abdullah narrated to us. He said: Abu Ja`far Ahmad b. Muhammad b. `Isa and Musa b. Ja`far b. Abi Ja`far al-Baghdadi narrated to us from Abi Talib `Abdullah b. Salt al-Qummi from al-Hasan b. `Ali b. Faddal from Dawud b. Abi Yazid. He said: Al-Sadiq Ja`far b. Muhammad (as) said:
When the Sun disappears, then Maghrib time has begun.
